diagnostics.message: module.crossplane:resource.kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config has `depends_on = [kubectl_manifest.aws_provider, time_sleep.wait_30_seconds]`, but time_sleep.wait_30_seconds already `depends_on = [kubectl_manifest.aws_provider]`. The ordering against kubectl_manifest.aws_provider is therefore already guaranteed transitively, making the direct depends_on on it redundant.

The AWS Provider ControllerConfig builds its `iam-role-arn` as a hand-constructed string "...role/${eks_cluster_id}-aws-provider-irsa" instead of referencing the IRSA role created by module.aws_provider_irsa. As a result it has no ordering on that IAM role (and the role module currently even depends on kubectl_manifest.aws_provider, i.e. it may be created after the provider is deployed). On first apply Crossplane can start the AWS provider pods before the role/trust policy the SA annotation points to exists, causing AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failures. Wire the ControllerConfig to the role ARN so the dependency is real.

The Terrajet Provider ControllerConfig builds its `iam-role-arn` as a hand-constructed string "...role/${eks_cluster_id}-jet-aws-provider-irsa" instead of referencing the IRSA role created by module.jet_aws_provider_irsa, so no ordering is established. On first apply the Terrajet provider pods can come up before that IAM role/trust policy exists, causing AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failures. Reference the role ARN so the dependency is real.
